description: A geographic bin map showing the number of Australia's 19 National Surfing Reserves within 2-degree longitude by 2-degree latitude cells.

usermeta.title: Where Do Recognised Surfing Reserves Cluster?
usermeta.annotation: Six reserves occupy the Sydney–Central Coast cell, accounting for 32% of the 19 registered National Surfing Reserves.
usermeta.analysis: Australia's 19 listed National Surfing Reserves occupy ten geographic grid cells of 2° longitude × 2° latitude. The largest concentration is between 150°–152°E and 34°–32°S, where six reserves—Maroubra, Bondi, North Narrabeen, Manly–Freshwater, Merewether and Norah Head—account for approximately 32% of the national register. A second cluster near the NSW–Queensland border includes Gold Coast, Lennox Head and Angourie, while Margaret River and Yallingup share a cell in southwest Western Australia. Other reserves are more geographically isolated, demonstrating that recognised surfing heritage extends beyond the main eastern coastal clusters. This distribution provides evidence of where formal recognition is concentrated, but does not establish which destinations have the best waves or attract the most visitors. Because the bins are equal in degrees rather than physical area or coastline length, their counts should not be interpreted as a normalised measure of surfing activity.
